# Research Data Collection Guide

## Artifacts Generated by Your Pipelines

Each CI/CD run generates artifacts stored for 90 days on GitHub.

---

## What Data is Available?

### From Backend Pipeline (`backend-ci-cd.yml`)
- **test-coverage-backend** - Jest coverage reports (JSON, HTML)
- **security-scan-results-backend** - TruffleHog, Gitleaks, Semgrep, CodeQL outputs
- **container-scan-results-backend** - Trivy, Grype, Dockle results
- **sarif-results-backend** - CodeQL, Semgrep SARIF files
- **research-metadata-backend** - Pipeline metrics, timestamps, build info

### From Python Pipeline (`python-ci-cd.yml`)
- **test-coverage-python** - Pytest coverage (JSON, XML, HTML)
- **security-scan-results-python** - Bandit, TruffleHog, Gitleaks, Semgrep outputs
- **container-scan-results-python** - Trivy, Grype, Dockle results
- **sarif-results-python** - Bandit, CodeQL, Semgrep SARIF files
- **research-metadata-python** - Pipeline metrics

### From Frontend Pipeline (`frontend-ci-cd.yml`)
- **test-coverage-frontend** - Vitest coverage reports
- **security-scan-results-frontend** - TruffleHog, Gitleaks, Semgrep, CodeQL outputs
- **container-scan-results-frontend** - Trivy, Grype, Dockle results
- **sarif-results-frontend** - CodeQL, Semgrep SARIF files
- **research-metadata-frontend** - Pipeline metrics

---

## Step-by-Step Download Process

### Step 1: Access Actions Tab

Go to: https://github.com/Gungnir44/devops-ml-security-and-anomaly-research/actions

You should see:
- ✅ **Backend CI/CD** (latest run)
- ✅ **Python CI/CD** (latest run)
- ✅ **Frontend CI/CD** (latest run)

### Step 2: Download Individual Run Artifacts

For EACH workflow run:

1. Click the workflow name (e.g., "Backend CI/CD")
2. Click the most recent run (green ✓ or red ✗)
3. Scroll to bottom → "Artifacts" section
4. Click each artifact to download ZIP

**Repeat for all 3 pipelines!**

### Step 3: Organize Downloaded Data

Create this folder structure on your machine:

```
C:\Users\joshu\Desktop\DevOps Project\research-data\
├── baseline-week-1\
│   ├── backend\
│   │   ├── security-scans\
│   │   ├── container-scans\
│   │   ├── test-coverage\
│   │   └── metadata\
│   ├── python\
│   │   ├── security-scans\
│   │   ├── container-scans\
│   │   ├── test-coverage\
│   │   └── metadata\
│   └── frontend\
│       ├── security-scans\
│       ├── container-scans\
│       ├── test-coverage\
│       └── metadata\
├── baseline-week-2\
├── baseline-week-3\
└── baseline-week-4\
```

### Step 4: Extract and Categorize

After downloading ZIPs:

```powershell
# Navigate to research data folder
cd "C:\Users\joshu\Desktop\DevOps Project\research-data\baseline-week-1"

# Extract each ZIP into appropriate folder
Expand-Archive -Path "security-scan-results-backend.zip" -DestinationPath "backend\security-scans"
Expand-Archive -Path "container-scan-results-backend.zip" -DestinationPath "backend\container-scans"
Expand-Archive -Path "test-coverage-backend.zip" -DestinationPath "backend\test-coverage"
```

## Alternative: Access SARIF Results Directly

### GitHub Security Tab

1. Go to: https://github.com/Gungnir44/devops-ml-security-and-anomaly-research/security/code-scanning

2. You'll see all security findings in a **browsable interface**:
   - Filter by tool (CodeQL, Semgrep)
   - Filter by severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low)
   - Filter by status (Open, Dismissed)
   - Filter by branch

3. **Export options:**
   - Click "Download CSV" for spreadsheet analysis
   - Use GitHub API for programmatic access (see below)

## Advanced: GitHub API for Bulk Download

### Using PowerShell + GitHub API

```powershell
# Set variables
$owner = "Gungnir44"
$repo = "devops-ml-security-and-anomaly-research"
$token = "YOUR_GITHUB_TOKEN"  # Create at: https://github.com/settings/tokens

# Get all workflow runs
$runs = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://api.github.com/repos/$owner/$repo/actions/runs" `
  -Headers @{Authorization = "token $token"}

# List latest run IDs
$runs.workflow_runs | Select-Object -First 5 | ForEach-Object {
  Write-Host "Run ID: $($_.id) - $($_.name) - $($_.conclusion)"
}

# Download artifacts for a specific run
$runId = 123456789  # Replace with actual run ID
$artifacts = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://api.github.com/repos/$owner/$repo/actions/runs/$runId/artifacts" `
  -Headers @{Authorization = "token $token"}

# Download each artifact
foreach ($artifact in $artifacts.artifacts) {
  $downloadUrl = $artifact.archive_download_url
  $filename = "$($artifact.name).zip"

  Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $downloadUrl `
    -Headers @{Authorization = "token $token"} `
    -OutFile $filename

  Write-Host "Downloaded: $filename"
}
```

### Create GitHub Token

1. Go to: https://github.com/settings/tokens
2. Click "Generate new token (classic)"
3. Select scopes: `repo`, `workflow`
4. Generate and save token securely

## What to Look For in Downloaded Data

### Security Scan Results (JSON/SARIF)

```json
{
  "tool": "semgrep",
  "findings": [
    {
      "rule_id": "javascript.express.security.audit.xss.mustache.explicit-unescape",
      "severity": "WARNING",
      "path": "sample-apps/backend-api/routes/users.js",
      "line": 42,
      "message": "Potential XSS vulnerability"
    }
  ]
}
```

**For your research:**
- Count findings by severity
- Track findings over time
- Categorize by CWE/OWASP
- Map to ML features (Feature #45: "Number of HIGH severity SAST findings")

### Container Scan Results

```json
{
  "tool": "trivy",
  "image": "ghcr.io/gungnir44/backend-api:latest",
  "vulnerabilities": [
    {
      "cve": "CVE-2024-1234",
      "severity": "HIGH",
      "package": "openssl",
      "installed_version": "1.1.1",
      "fixed_version": "1.1.1w"
    }
  ]
}
```

**For your research:**
- Track CVE trends
- Dependency vulnerability patterns
- Map to Feature #67-72 (Dependency metrics)

### Test Coverage Data

```json
{
  "coverage": {
    "lines": 78.5,
    "statements": 76.2,
    "functions": 82.1,
    "branches": 71.3
  }
}
```

**For your research:**
- Code quality metrics
- Correlation with security findings
- Map to Feature #12-15 (Code coverage features)

## Quick Start Checklist

- [ ] Go to GitHub Actions tab
- [ ] Click first workflow run (Backend CI/CD)
- [ ] Scroll to Artifacts section
- [ ] Download all artifacts (4-5 files)
- [ ] Repeat for Python CI/CD workflow
- [ ] Repeat for Frontend CI/CD workflow
- [ ] Extract ZIPs to research-data folder
- [ ] Open JSON/SARIF files in text editor
- [ ] Import into Excel/Python for analysis

---

## Automation Tip

Since pipelines run weekly, set a reminder to download artifacts every Monday:

1. **Week 1-4**: Baseline data collection
2. **Week 5-8**: After implementing attack scenarios
3. **Week 9-12**: After ML model deployment

This gives you **before, during, after** datasets for thesis!
